concept.name: After-hours session
concept.definition: Extended-hours trading that occurs after the regular session closes; per the SEC, after-hours trading (also called extended-hours trading) is trading outside regular trading hours, which for U.S. exchange-listed stocks end at 4:00 p.m. ET. Late sessions on U.S. equity venues typically run until 8:00 p.m. ET.
concept.intuition: Trading continues after the closing bell, letting investors react to late news, but in a thinner, jumpier market.
concept.mechanics: After the closing cross completes in a stock, after-hours trading commences on ECNs and exchange late sessions with reduced order-type support and no LULD bands; executions report to the tape but do not change the official closing price.
concept.failure_modes: Low volume and wide spreads make after-hours prices unreliable guides to the next day's open; a stock can move sharply on a few hundred shares, and stop or market orders can fill at extreme prices.
concept.misconceptions: An after-hours trade does not change 'the closing price' — the official close was set by the 4:00 p.m. closing auction — and after-hours gains or losses frequently reverse at the next open.
concept.example: A company issues a profit warning at 4:30 p.m. ET; the stock drops 12% in the after-hours session on light volume, while the tape's official closing price remains the 4:00 p.m. cross.

citations.source: Nasdaq, The Nasdaq Opening and Closing Crosses FAQ
citations.section: Section 5 (after-hours trading commences as the Closing Cross completes)
